So here in my 3D window, I have this really cool garment. And what I can do is I can decide which aspects of the garment I want to see based off of what's selected. And I can do that using this really cool new feature in my 3D toggle menu over here. And it's this new feature right here. It's called isolate selection. So if I hover over, you're going to see isolate selection. Shift I. That's the shortcut. Now, if I turn it on right now, everything will disappear because nothing's selected. All I have to do is select something. So let's say I just want to see that shirt underneath the jacket. So I'm going to double click on this, zoom out, and now I'm going to select this. And now I just see the shirt. I can click away and now I can just see this shirt really quickly and easily. And I can zoom in, check out how it is. You know, maybe I want to simulate. Move this around. Adjust it a bit. Or anything like that. Now, I can turn this off and then see the whole thing. And again, I could double click maybe on this whole jacket. And then just see what the jacket's like without the shirt or the jeans. See how I like that. Maybe I want to show. Maybe I want to like. Again. If I wanted to, I could simulate. Move this around. Nose. And if I want to again, see my whole outfit together, all I have to do is go back over to this tool. Turn it off and then I'll see everything. And why not? Let's just do it for the jeans. I'm going to double click on these jeans. Quick and easy. And then I can just click away really, really helpful to help you see different aspects of your whole garment, or if you wanted to see the inside or the outside, like maybe I wanted to select just this edge here, you know, and maybe these panels, right? And then I can turn this on. And now I can see the inside of this. And then turn it off. Great. Really, really helpful, right? If you have any questions, use that comment section down below. Don't forget to like, and subscribe lots of great videos for you to like go and learn more. And all of that stuff, keep having fun and grow and things again.
markdown_content: ## Isolate Selection Mode (CLO 2026.0) in the 3D Window This section introduces **Isolate Selection** as a new feature in the **3D toggle menu** for inspecting specific parts of a garment. It lets you control what’s visible in the 3D window based on what you select. In the **3D window**, you can choose which aspects of a garment to see using the **Isolate Selection** tool found in the **3D toggle menu**. The feature is labeled **Isolate Selection**, and it has a keyboard shortcut: **Shift + I**. When you enable **Isolate Selection** while nothing is selected, the result is that **everything disappears**. To use it effectively, you must first select an element of the garment (e.g., a shirt, jacket, jeans, edge, or panel). Once something is selected, turning the tool on isolates that selected part for focused inspection. ## Using the Shift + I Shortcut to Isolate a Selected Part This section explains the practical workflow: select an object, enable isolate selection, and then toggle it off to return to the full view. 1. **Enable Isolate Selection** using **Shift + I** (or the toggle in the 3D menu). 2. **Select something first**—otherwise, enabling the tool will hide everything. 3. To isolate a garment component, for example the **shirt under a jacket**: - **Double-click** the shirt area (or the relevant component). - **Zoom out** if needed to locate the part. - **Select** the component you want isolated. 4. With isolate selection active, you can quickly verify the isolated part in the viewport: - Click away to confirm isolation behavior. - **Zoom in** to inspect details. - **Simulate moving** the component around (e.g., reposition to view it from different angles). 5. When you’re done inspecting, **turn off** isolate selection to see the **whole garment** again. ## Double-Click Isolation for Jacket vs. Shirt/Jeans This section shows how isolate selection works when isolating larger garment pieces via double-click selection. You can also isolate bigger components, such as a **jacket**. For example: - **Double-click** the **jacket**. - Turn on **Isolate Selection** to view the jacket without other garment parts (e.g., without the shirt or jeans). - Toggle the feature off to return to the full outfit view. This same approach can be repeated for other items like **jeans**, enabling quick comparisons between individual garment pieces and the full assembled outfit. ## Inspecting Inside/Outside Surfaces with Edge and Panel Selection This section describes isolating more granular geometry selections—such as edges and panels—to inspect interior or exterior surfaces. Isolate selection is not limited to whole garments. You can also isolate finer details, such as: - **Edges** - **Panels** For example, to inspect the **inside** of the garment: 1. Select the relevant **edge** and/or **panels** that correspond to the region you want to view. 2. Turn on **Isolate Selection**. 3. The viewport will show only the selected interior region (e.g., the inside panels/sections). 4. Turn the tool off to return to the full view. This is useful for checking how different parts of the garment relate to each other and for verifying construction details on specific surfaces.
